text:
alex_w: heads-up - Acme reported duplicate final tokens after reconnect and they were billed twice for the same completion. seeing two final chunks both containing the last 5 tokens.

mira_s: ack, can you paste logs + pcap? rough symptoms?

alex_w: symptoms: client streaming SSE, connection drops mid-stream, client resumes immediately with resume-token, then receives the tail again (duplicate). billing shows two completion units for one logical completion.

samir_k: do we have edge proxy logs or Instance IDs? any 101/keepalive noise?

alex_w: uploaded pcap: s3://acme-support/pcap/2249012345_acme.pcap

alex_w: tcpdump snippet:
```
13:02:10.123 IP client->edge: FIN, ack
13:02:10.125 IP edge->client: keepalive (no ack seen)
13:02:10.200 IP client->edge: GET /stream?resume_token=abc123 (resume)
13:02:10.201 IP edge->backend: new request routing to same model cluster
13:02:10.276 IP backend->edge: streamed tail tokens (duplicate)
```

mira_s: interesting — looks like the resume created a distinct request on a different instance. do we have kvcache logs?

alex_w: original request-id: req_9fd2, resume req-id: req_9fd2-resume. backend log snippet:
```
[13:02:10.120] req_9fd2: emit token seq 1..198
[13:02:10.250] req_9fd2-resume: KV not found -> warming kvcache -> emit tail seq 199..203
```

samir_k: "KV not found" is the smoking gun. TTL for kvcache is 30s — why routed to instance without the cached KV? routing policy or instance affinity race likely.

jessica_p: customer uses mobile SDK that does very fast reconnects. alex, can you share a minimal curl repro we can run locally?

alex_w: repro steps (minimal):
```
# open initial stream
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-xl" > out1.txt &
# wait for partial output then kill connection (simulate flaky mobile)
sleep 2; kill $!  # simulate network drop
# immediately resume
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-resume-token: abc123" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-xl" > out2.txt
# inspect out1.txt and out2.txt for duplicate tail tokens
```

mira_s: please gather traces and edge route ids for both requests. we need trace ids, edge-route ID, and instance IDs to correlate.

alex_w: trace ids: trace=trace-9fd2, resume-trace=trace-9fd2-resume; edge-route=edge-a1; instance ids: inst-03 (orig) and inst-07 (resume).

samir_k: likely race where kvcache hadn't replicated to inst-07. fallback path emitted missing continuation as a fresh generation, causing duplicate tokens + double billing. mitigation options: pin resume to original instance when possible, or add resume de-dup at router based on request id + seq.

mira_s: action items: eng-runtime to investigate kvcache replication lag and resume routing (assign to @samir_k). ops to pull pcap + token emission metrics (tokens_emitted per request). support to send customer repro steps + temporary mitigation. :thumbsup:

eng_support_bot: incident created: INC-2024-455 ; assignees: @samir_k, @eng-runtime ; priority: P2

alex_w: customer notified with repro and temp mitigation: add 100-200ms jitter before resuming to reduce likelihood of racing into an instance without kvcache. they accepted this workaround for now.

mira_s: thanks — please keep updates here as eng digs in.
